lines.n_stats: Seventy-six percent of shoppers prefer to buy in their own language. Translation fixes the words. It doesn't fix the references.
lines.n_copy: So here's my real copy, with its very European hooks — and three rooms to win: Tokyo, Brussels, and Austin.
lines.n_run: One click. The agent asks Qloo what each room actually loves — artists, films, books, brands, places — filtered by city and age.
lines.n_log: This is a live run, not a mockup. Every reference gets tested against Qloo's taste data, and every replacement must come from what Qloo returned in this very run. The agent cannot invent a reference. Grounded, or rejected.
lines.n_verdict: The verdict: three rewrites, each with its taste facts — the exact Qloo entities, and their affinity scores, behind every swap.
lines.n_brussels: And there's the worse: Brussels dropped my praline line entirely. Comparing my bar to the city's own praline starts a contest with local chocolate — a fight no translation tool would have seen.
lines.n_honest: And when Qloo has no data — Port wine, or a Willemstad audience — my agent says so. Flagged, never faked.
lines.n_outro: Lengua Fina. Every reference, traceable to Qloo. Built for the Qloo Agentic Hackathon.
